Formulation:
Predisposing: Personal tendency toward high-pressure careers; underlying thyroid disorder.  
Precipitating: Recent job change with increased workload and stress.  
Perpetuating: Ongoing high job demands, prolonged computer use, possible thyroid hormone excess exacerbating autonomic arousal.  
Protective: Help-seeking behaviour; stable employment; limited alcohol use.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Work-related stress / possible anxiety
- Patient Goal(s): Reduce daily stress level; improve sense of control at work; decrease physical anxiety symptoms
- Clinical Goal(s): Clarify anxiety diagnosis; reduce symptom frequency/intensity; improve overall functioning
- Actions (Patient):
  • Book in-person GP appointment as advised  
  • Begin daily stress-reduction strategy (e.g., brief mindfulness exercise 5 min x2/day)  
  • Schedule regular breaks from screen work; ergonomic adjustments
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  • Full physical exam and thyroid function tests to rule out/confirm hyperthyroidism  
  • Administer GAD-7 and PHQ-9 screening tools at next visit  
  • Provide brief psychoeducation on stress management; consider referral for CBT if anxiety confirmed

Secondary Problem: Possible iatrogenic hyperthyroidism
- Patient Goal(s): Understand thyroid status; alleviate heat intolerance and palpitations
- Clinical Goal(s): Achieve euthyroid state; distinguish endocrine vs. psychological symptom drivers
- Actions (Patient): Continue current thyroxine until reviewed; report any symptom escalation
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Order TSH, free T4/T3; review thyroxine dose; consider endocrinology referral

Tertiary Problem: Tension/migraine-type headaches
- Patient Goal(s): Fewer headaches; maintain work productivity
- Clinical Goal(s): Identify headache triggers; provide non-pharmacological and pharmacological options if required
- Actions (Patient): Headache diary (time, activity, severity); trial regular hydration and posture changes
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Assess for migraine features; counsel on over-the-counter analgesic use; consider preventative strategies after thyroid/anxiety work-up

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Link between stress, thyroid function, and somatic symptoms; importance of in-person review and labs
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increased frequency of palpitations/SOB; escalating headaches; further weight loss; emerging low mood
- Coping Strategies: Scheduled breaks, mindfulness, physical activity, maintaining balanced meals

Consent, Coordination & Review:
- Patient Consent to Plan: Yes (verbal)
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: To be provided at next in-person visit
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: None currently
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not applicable
- Review Date: Within 4–6 weeks post-laboratory results or sooner if symptoms escalate

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Iatrogenic hyperthyroidism – Likelihood: High. On thyroxine with classic hyper-thyroid symptoms.
- Stress-related anxiety/panic disorder – Likelihood: Medium. Symptoms occur during high-stress work periods; autonomic features present.
- Tension or migraine-type headaches – Likelihood: Medium. Frontal headaches with screen-time association and mild nausea.

Quality checks
● Missing but clinically expected elements: Sleep pattern, detailed suicidal risk assessment, family psychiatric history, emergency contact information.  
● Internal conflicts: Patient states “hyperthyroidism” yet is taking thyroxine (replacement for hypothyroidism) – conflict noted.  
● Transcript quality notes: Several audio gaps; dates and certain details (address, contact) not captured in transcript.
